classification.difficultyReason: The student must deduce x=±2 from the height 5 on the curve, integrate the area under the parabola, and subtract the rectangle. This is a routine linked procedure like the rectangle-minus-arch question p9-q4a, with one inference to make.

content.prompt: Find the area of the shaded region.

answer.worked:
The curve meets the $x$-axis where $9-x^2=0$, so $x=\pm3$. The top corners of the rectangle lie on the curve at height $5$:
$$\begin{align*}9-x^2&=5\\x^2&=4\\x&=\pm2\end{align*}$$
The rectangle is $4$ wide and $5$ high, so its area is $20$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\int_{-3}^{3}(9-x^2)\,dx-20\\&=\left[9x-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^{3}-20\\&=36-20\\&=16\text{ u}^2\end{align*}$$
